newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says peso policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says peso policy unchanged.

text.p: The Philippines' foreign exchange policy has not been changed, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday.
"(The rate) shall not be administratively fixed but shall be determined through transactions in the foreign exchange market on a day-to-day basis," he said in a statement.

The Central Bank raised overnight borrowing rates to 30 percent earlier from 24 percent after an "unusual" increase in currency trading following a report in a Singapore newspaper quoting the Philippine Finance Secretary as saying the peso may be devalued, the statement said.
It said the interest rate rise was designed to counter speculation against the peso.
The peso has come under heavy attack this month following the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht, with some investors saying the Philippine currency could be next.
Singson reiterated that the authorities would intervene in the market to compensate for "excessive fluctuations" or counter a speculative attack on the peso.
"(The Central Bank's) actions today reflect what it is prepared to do when the currency comes under speculative pressures," the statement added.
